ideas.name: Scope change approval ledger
ideas.job: Turn an out-of-scope request into an explicit priced decision before work starts
ideas.wedge: Compare original deliverable against change and preserve client decision without moving project tools
ideas.channel: Permission-based agency operator community post offering a change-control worksheet; invite opt-in walkthroughs. Partner hypothesis: fractional agency operations consultants with existing clients. No access or conversions verified.
ideas.risk: Ignition directly offers the core approval flow; an additional USD 49 subscription may be worse than configuring an existing suite.
ideas.reason: Reserve after direct-feature falsification: incumbent change orders closely match the proposition. Advance only if buyers cannot migrate existing agreement/billing systems and will pay for a standalone approval layer.
ideas.mvp: Original scope import, change form, approve/defer link and evidence export
ideas.validation: With ten agencies outside Ignition, compare a redacted scope change in their current workflow, Ignition documentation and a standalone prototype; require three priced pilot commitments and repeat use.
ideas.competitors: Ignition client-approved change orders directly cover scope and price changes; Bonsai agreements; email plus a shared change log.
ideas.pricing_test: Proposed USD 49/month per organization;14-day bounded trial, no permanent free file hosting. Paid boundary: repeated cycles, reusable templates and shared evidence history. Test annual 10-month-equivalent plan only after repeated use; lifetime would leave ongoing reminders/support unfunded.
ideas.cost_risk: Analyst design assumption: cap pilot at 5 GB files,1000 active records and 1000 notifications/month; use links/CSV before APIs. Sensitive-data handling and onboarding support may exceed hosting cost; measure support minutes before estimating margin. Budget gate: MVP recurring operating spend must fit USD 20–50/month per product before revenue; use shared low-cost hosting, deterministic rules and email caps. This is a budget constraint, not a measured quote. Defer paid APIs, sensitive file hosting and expensive integrations until revenue permits roughly USD 300/month/product; never buy them merely to complete a prototype.
ideas.global_note: English-language initial workflow; customer supplies policies and dates. Data residency, consent, payment availability and localized templates require country-by-country checks; no legal/tax/compliance outcome is promised.
ideas.kill_test: Stop if three of ten qualified agencies can solve the problem by configuring current tools within one hour, or fewer than three accept a USD 49 pilot after seeing that comparison.
